children: North Sea operations have drawn interest from suitors including Adura, an Equinor-Shell
joint venture, and NEO Next+, backed by TotalEnergies
, and HitecVision, Bloomberg reported Wednesday, as the oil company seeks to exit the region even as the U.K. government hints at allowing more drilling there.
Other potential bidders that may study the assets include EnQuest
Bloomberg reported in May that BP

was considering a sale of its operations in the North Sea, which could be valued at ~£2B ($2.7B) in a full divestment, as the area has become less attractive to the oil industry in part due to U.K. tax policy for the sector and government restrictions on exploration and development of new projects.
New U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has suggested his administration could allow more drilling, but BP
CEO Meg O'Neill said last month that any further shifts in policy would not sway her decision to sell.
